extracted.intended_audience: practitioners before the USPTO (particularly Canadian attorneys who represent trademark applicants), OED/USPTO staff, and attorneys interested in USPTO disciplinary standards
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order describing the facts, legal conclusions, applicable regulations, and agreed sanctions for a Canadian attorney who filed trademark applications for applicants not located in Canada. The page sets out regulatory limits on Canadian practitioners, specific rule violations, procedural enforcement steps, and publication/recording requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites statutory and regulatory authority for issuing disciplinary orders and approving settlement agreements; establishes the Office's power to adjudicate practitioner misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO disciplinary rules and professional conduct rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq. and the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct found at 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 through 11.901.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which regulatory regimes govern practitioner conduct (the older Code of Professional Responsibility for events before May 3, 2013 and the Rules of Professional Conduct for events on/after May 3, 2013).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of Canadian attorneys to represent clients before the USPTO (37 C.F.R. § 11.14(c) / § 10.14(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Canadian attorneys authorized under 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(c) (or its predecessor § 10.14(c)) may represent individuals and business entities located in Canada before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the scope of practice for Canadian practitioners to Canadian-located individuals and entities; the Final Order reiterates this territorial limitation as the basis for misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on representing Canadian nationals or entities not located in Canada (TMEP § 602.03(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Canadian attorneys may not represent a Canadian national who resides in the United States but has access to a mailing address in Canada; nor may they represent a business entity unless its corporate domicile or principal place of business is in Canada.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies edge cases (e.g., Canadian nationals resident in the U.S. with Canadian mailing addresses; business entities without domicile/principal place of business in Canada) to determine whether representation is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misrepresentation / false declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting and signing a declaration stating '[t]he signatory has confirmed that he/she is a Canadian attorney/agent, or an associate thereof, who represents an applicant located in Canada....' when that statement is false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signing a false statement regarding the applicant's location (or the signatory's authority) is misconduct subject to disciplinary action; the Final Order cites three applications where this false statement was made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) (pre-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before May 3, 2013, representing before the Office trademark applicants who are not located in Canada violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Respondent acknowledged this violation based on stipulated facts that he filed applications for owners not located in Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d) (post-May 3, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: After May 3, 2013, continuing to represent before the Office trademark applicants who are not located in Canada violates 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Respondent acknowledged this post-rule-change violation where he continued representation even after a disciplinary complaint was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprimand and probation as disciplinary sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is reprimanded and shall serve a one year probationary period commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the concrete sanctions imposed: formal reprimand plus one-year probation; during probation Respondent's practice rights are limited as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited practice rights during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be permitted to practice trademark law on behalf of individuals and companies located in Canada before the USPTO during his probationary period unless his probation is revoked and he is suspended by order of the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that during probation the territorial restriction remains in force; violation during probation may trigger further enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED enforcement procedure during probation (Order to Show Cause and suspension process)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent, grant 15 calendar days to respond, and may then deliver materials to the USPTO Director requesting suspension of up to 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details stepwise enforcement: (i) Order to Show Cause, (ii) 15 days to respond, (iii) OED may forward record and request immediate suspension for up to 30 days; any review of suspension does not stay effect of suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette (Notice of Reprimand and Probation) with specified explanatory language about the misconduct and limitations on practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates public notice of the discipline and provides the notice text summarizing the violation and scope of authorized practice for Canadian attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct or in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that the record can be relied upon in future enforcement or disciplinary decisions and may aggravate future sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement to dismiss pending disciplinary proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall file a joint motion dismissing the USPTO disciplinary proceeding pending against Respondent within fourteen days after entry of any Final Order approving this Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the timeframe and action required to conclude the pending administrative proceeding as part of the settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement term allocating legal/administrative costs between the parties.
